function: Learned RIS/SIM phase configuration plus transceiver encoder/decoder, trained end-to-end for over-the-air edge inference (image classification) over a MIMO link. p. 7-8
system: Uplink MIMO, Nt=2-12 TX antennas, Nr=32 RX; reflecting RIS (16x16 to 25x25) or stacked SIM (3 layers of 8x8 to 12x12); narrowband 28 GHz. p. 11-12
method: Encoder/decoder DNNs (convolutional, linear layers) plus MS controller DNN or trainable fixed phases; supervised end-to-end backpropagation through the channel (Adam, cross-entropy); TX-power fine-tuning. p. 8, 12, 14
data_channel: MNIST, F-MNIST, K-MNIST, CIFAR-10 images; simulated Ricean MIMO channels at 28 GHz per ref. [35]; 10^4 training and 10^3 testing channel realizations. p. 11-12
test_conditions: Same Ricean setup, disjoint test channels and images; separate training per Nt, MS size, dataset; noisy-CSI test; TX power lowered from 30 to -20 dBm by fine-tuning. p. 12-14
baselines: No-MS end-to-end DNN (same encoder/decoder, Phi=0); RX-DNN: VAE, K-PSK, SVD precoding, WMMSE combining, RIS phases by projected gradient ascent on rate, pretrained classifier. p. 12, 15-16
metrics: Classification accuracy (mean, standard deviation, best of restarts); TX computational energy per inference instance (mJ) from measured GPU power and latency. p. 12, 15
complexity: Trainable DNN parameters per variant in Table I (2.5x10^5 to 2.5x10^7); TX energy and inference latency in Table II (e.g., MNIST 2.39 mJ, 3.62 s). p. 12, 15
openness: Code released at https://github.com/NoesysLab/Metasurfaces-Integrated-Neural-Networks (footnote, p. 2); datasets are public torchvision sets, channels simulated.
q1_support: p. 11: "Narrowband transmissions at 28 GHz with varying Ricean fading conditions were considered". Custom simulator following ref. [35] (Ricean, ULA/URA, free-space path loss); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channels are used, so not met.
q2_support: p. 14: "decreasing the transmission power by 5 dBm every five epochs". Only TX power (SNR) and CSI error (p. 13) change; other Nt, MS sizes and datasets are trained separately (p. 12), so no new scenario, band or dataset is tested; not met.
q3_support: p. 12: "a baseline of the same encoder and decoder modules, but in the absence of any MS". This no-MS baseline is the proposed MINN with Phi=0 (an ablation). Non-learned baseline is met by RX-DNN (classical rate-maximizing RIS/precoder optimization, p. 15-16), but no independent earlier learned method is compared; not met.
q4_support: p. 12: "The numbers of trainable parameters for all considered MINN versions are included in Table I". Table I gives parameter counts; Table II (p. 15) gives TX energy per instance and measured inference latency.
q5_support: p. 2: "The code for this paper is available at https://github.com/NoesysLab/". Footnote 1 gives the full link (Metasurfaces-Integrated-Neural-Networks); MNIST/CIFAR-10 alone would not count.
notes: Title and DOI on page 1 match the file. Included in area 3: the learned part includes the RIS/SIM phases (controller DNN, p. 7, or trained static phases, p. 8) jointly with the transceiver DNNs for goal-oriented edge inference; not federated aggregation. Flags for the reviewer: (1) q2 is 0 because the power-decrement fine-tuning (p. 14, framed by the authors as transfer learning) changes only TX power, i.e. an SNR sweep. (2) q3 is 0 because the no-MS baseline is an ablation (p. 12) although p. 5 says it is the setup of ref. [7] as a special case of MINN; if the reviewer accepts it as the earlier learned method of [7], q3 becomes 1.
